children: shares slid 4.76% 10.15 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, extending Friday's 4.76% drop. The pressure traces to Rothschild & Co Redburn, which downgraded Broadcom to Neutral from Buy, citing reliance on credit-fueled AI deals with clients such as Anthropic and OpenAI. TIKR reported the price target fell to $398 from $595.

Redburn's argument is about timing, not demand. The firm said the labs must establish lasting primacy over open models and become self-financing quickly, and that upside from clearing those hurdles is unlikely to arrive fast. Management has guided to about $115 billion of AI revenue in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028, according to the same TIKR summary. Broadcom is also writing its own check: Anthropic's amended S-1 lists Broadcom as a buyer of 13,513,513 placement shares, about $1 billion at the $74 midpoint.

That circularity is the risk in one line: a supplier funding a customer that funds the supplier's backlog. Even after the cut, Redburn's $398 target sits about 19% above today's price. GuruFocus scores Broadcom 98/100 on elite margins and strong growth, with financial strength the softer spot. Shares trade about 26% below the $451.72 GF Value, a modestly undervalued reading, and GuruFocus shows a forward P/E near 17. Cheap on forecasts only works if the forecasts survive. Broadcom's fiscal fourth-quarter report in December is the next proof point on AI revenue conversion.

title: Broadcom Stocks Slide 4.76% as Downgrade Keeps AI Financing Fears in Focus
